To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
concanavalins induce apoptosis of cancer cells lacking p53 and that p53 expression protects them by inducing G(0)/G(1) arrest.

Con A-induced apoptosis of ovarian cancer cells is p53-dependent and is mediated by up-regulation of FOXO1a/Bim signaling, which is strongly inhibited after p54 expression and rescued after its ablation.

Con A induces FOXO1a/Bim-mediated apoptosis of cells lacking wild-type p53 and that p53 protects these cancer cells from apoptosis by inducing G(0)-G(1) cell cycle arrest and by down-regulating FOXO1a expression.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of p53 and p73 in the induction of apoptosis and the mechanism of their cross-talk.
the role of p53 and p53-related proteins, p73 and FOXO1a, in the regulation of cell cycle arrest and apoptosis.
the molecular mechanisms by which p53 protects against Con A-induced apoptosis and provides a new insight into the role of p53 and FOXO1a in apoptosis

the restoration of p53 function protects cells from Con A-induced apoptosis.

p53 is an essential regulator in protecting cells from concanvalin A-induced apoptosis.

p53 is a critical factor in protection against Con A-induced apoptosis and that the FOXO1a pathway is a novel target for cancer therapy.
